object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books and attends medical appointments at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a patient, displayed on their card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who sees patients and is assigned specialties.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor... Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a doctor's medical license.

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at the clinic.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an appointment, assigned when created.

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room at the clinic used for patient examinations.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for an exam room.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty, such as cardiology or general practice.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot for appointment scheduling, such as 09:00 or 09:30.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled. Never. An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

object_types.name: VisitReason
object_types.definition: The reason provided by the patient for scheduling an appointment.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.

object_types.name: FollowUpNote
object_types.definition: A note attached by the doctor to an appointment following the patient visit.

source_references.excerpt: After the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note.

ambiguities.description: Uniqueness of appointment date and time slot combination: The transcript does not explicitly state whether the combination of AppointmentDate and TimeSlot must be unique (i.e., whether only one Appointment can occur in a given room/doctor slot at a given time). This is implied by clinic operations (avoiding double-booking), but the constraint is not stated. Should we infer that the composite of (Doctor, AppointmentDate, TimeSlot) must be unique?

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Exam room assignment: The transcript mentions exam rooms but does not state whether an Appointment is assigned to an ExamRoom, or whether room assignment is separate from the appointment concept. Should there be a fact type 'Appointment is in ExamRoom'?

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor independence: The transcript states 'every patient has exactly one primary doctor' and notes it is 'separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment'. However, it is unclear whether a patient's primary doctor can be anyone (any Doctor in the system) or only doctors at this clinic, and whether the primary doctor relationship is independent of the appointment-doctor relationship or should have additional constraints (e.g., if a patient sees a doctor in an appointment, must that doctor be their primary doctor, or can they see other doctors?). The current model allows complete independence.

source_references.excerpt: That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.

ambiguities.description: Specialty uniqueness: The model infers that each Doctor has exactly one Specialty, but does not constrain whether multiple Doctors can have the same Specialty. The transcript implies many doctors can share a specialty (e.g., 'like cardiology or general practice'), which is captured by no uniqueness on the Specialty role. This is modeled correctly, but the assumption that Specialty is a value type (not an entity type with its own identifier) should be confirmed -- are specialties pre-defined codes or free text?

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.
